title: go-mutants trace event v1
description: One line of a go-mutants trace stream. A trace is the diagnostic account of a run, never evidence: it takes no part in a verdict, in a mutant identity, or in the key a cached result is stored under, and it records environment variable names without their values. See docs/trace-v1.md for the contract and docs/adr/0001-trace-is-not-evidence.md for why it is shaped this way.

seq.description: Position of the event in the recording, counting from one.

type.description: Which event this is, and therefore which payload it carries.

schema.description: Format identity, carried by the run-start event alone.

timestamp.description: When the event was recorded, RFC 3339 in UTC.

elapsed_ms.description: Milliseconds between the start of the recording and the event.

allOf.description: The type names the payload the line carries. Stated in this direction, a type with its payload missing is refused.

then.description: A phase is only timed when it ends, so a phase-start that carried a duration would describe a span nothing measured.
A phase-end always carries its duration, including when it is zero, so a reader can tell a phase that took under a millisecond from an event that was lost.

allOf.description: A payload appears only on the event type it belongs to. Stated in this direction, a line carrying two payloads — or somebody else's — is refused, so a reader may switch on the type and reach for that payload alone.

start.description: Who opened the recording, and what it is about.

kind.description: A CLI run, or a library workspace. They differ in what they can say about themselves: a run has a run id and an argument vector, a workspace has neither.

run_id.description: The run identity the report is also named by, so a recording and a report can be paired.

then.description: A workspace is opened by a program rather than by a command line, so it has neither a run id nor an argument vector to record.

phase.description: A phase of a run. A phase is only timed when it ends.

stage.description: One step inside a phase, recorded as a started/finished pair. The phase is stamped by the recorder from the phase that was open when the stage started, so no call site can mislabel one.

then.description: A started stage has produced neither a result nor a duration yet.
A finished stage always carries its duration, including when it is zero, so a reader can tell a fast stage from an event that was lost.

prepare.description: One timed stage of a library mutation session's preparation. Its fields and its vocabulary are goatest's, exactly, so one timeline reads the same in both recordings.

exec.description: One executed command, recorded after the child was reaped and recorded without its environment values and without its captured output.

kind.description: What the command was. Every subprocess go-mutants starts is labelled with one of these, so an unlabelled command is a recording that does not validate rather than a command a reader has to guess about.

subject.description: What the command was about: a mutant id, an import path, a scope pattern, or the name of the library call that issued it — absent when the kind says everything there is to say.

argv.description: The complete argument vector, exactly as the child received it: argv[0] is the executable, and the rest are the arguments it was given. Never null — a command that could not be run is recorded with the vector as it was given, which is the empty one when it had none.

env_names.description: Environment variable names alone, sorted and deduplicated: an item holding a value is not a trace.

then.description: A preserved output file is only meaningful beside the digest of the capture it holds part of.
Truncation is a property of the preserved file, so it is recorded only where there is one.

mutant.description: One attempt at one mutant. It shares id, display_id, package, args, timeout_ms, outcome, killed_by, duration_ms and error with goatest's own mutant record.

display_id.description: The short identity go-mutants names the mutant by: a prefix of `id` of `mutation.DisplayIDLength` characters, which is 20 today and is a constant the project may change. The bound is deliberately loose rather than pinned to that number, because a pattern that pinned it would turn a change to a display length into a recording nothing accepts.

attempt.description: Which attempt this is, from one: 1 is the concurrent pass, 2 the serial retry a survivor gets. Recorded rather than collapsed, because 'survived' and 'survived twice' are different facts about a flaky test.

worker.description: Which execution slot ran it, from zero.

binaries.description: The test binaries this attempt ran, in order, by the import path of the package each was built from — never the file that was executed, which is what the argv of the exec event underneath it carries. The import path is the name the run report uses and the one that outlives the temporary directory the file lived in.

outcome.description: What became of the attempt, in the vocabulary the library's Outcome uses: killed, survived, timed_out, inconclusive, errored, not_run. It is deliberately not an enum here, so that a recording made by an older build stays readable when the vocabulary grows.

killed_by.description: The test binary that detected the mutant, by the same import path binaries uses and the same one the run report's killed_by carries. It is one of binaries, so a reader can join the two.

exec_seqs.description: The exec events of the binaries this attempt ran, in order. They are how an attempt is joined to the commands underneath it, and therefore to their preserved output.

output_tail.description: The tail of the killing binary's output. It is stripped before a bounded ring and kept by a sink that writes to disk.

probe.description: One pass through the prepared probe tree, where no mutant is active and what is measured is which mutants' sites ever differed.

binaries.description: The test binaries the pass ran, by import path, exactly as a mutant record names them.

outcome.description: What became of the pass. Absent only on one carrying the error that stopped it instead.

infected.description: The mutants whose site the pass made differ, by full identity, each named once.

then.description: Only a measured pass observed anything, so the infections it recorded come with the outcome that measured them.

A measured pass always says what it infected, the empty list included: a measured pass that infected nothing is the strongest thing the probe phase says about a binary — nothing it runs can observe any of them — and omitting the list would make that claim indistinguishable from a pass nothing measured.

validate.description: One step of establishing which catalogued mutants can exist: the instrumentation, each compile, and each step of the bisection a red compile starts.

op.description: instrument wrote the catalogue into the tree; build compiled it once; gate found the tree broken with no mutant in it, which validation refuses to blame on a candidate; isolate searched one file; reject removed one candidate; done closed validation with what it spent and decided.

then.description: A rejection always names the candidate it removed.
A compile is numbered, so that a reader counting the compiles of one validation counts them the same way validation does.

coverage.description: How coverage placed one mutant: which test binaries reach the block the mutation sits in, or that none does.

start_line.description: The coverage block the mutation was mapped into, not the mutation's own span. Zero for a mutant whose position no block contained.

covering.description: The test binaries whose coverage profile reaches that block, by import path — the same identity a mutant record's binaries uses, and the same one the run report's covering_test_packages carries.

uncovered.description: The same statement as an empty covering set, recorded explicitly so that a reader is not asked to infer a decision from an omitted array.

then.description: A mutant no binary reaches has no covering binaries to name.

cache.description: One cache decision. A hit is the one event that explains an absence of work, which is why a warm run's recording is as long as it is.

outcome.description: The cached verdict a hit produced.

context_key.description: The identity the entry is filed under: `cache.Context.ContextKey()`, which is the full key truncated to `cache.ContextKeyLength` characters — the directory name, not the whole digest. No trace option enters it, which is why a traced and an untraced run share a cache.

then.description: A lookup and a store are always about one mutant; opening the store is about none.

stable.description: Whether the copy carried the source tree's modification times with it, which is what lets the Go build cache be reused across snapshots.

sweep.description: What collection reclaimed from a temporary directory before the run wrote anything into it. It is silent about a machine with nothing to reclaim, and it can never change a verdict.

live.description: Directories collection left alone because a running process still holds their lock.

kept.description: Directories collection left alone because a --keep-temp asked it to.

artifact.description: A file or directory the run wrote or kept.

note.description: Something the run could not do, said once. A note can never change a verdict.

code.description: The GOMnnnn code the run also reported to its console, where there is one.

run.description: The end of a recording, with the accounting that tells a complete trace from a lossy one.

events_emitted.description: Events the sink kept before this one. The accounting is taken before this event is written, so it excludes the run-end itself — goatest's rule too, so one number means one thing in both recordings. For an intact recording, events_emitted + events_dropped + 1 is the number of lines in the stream, with events_dropped zero.

events_dropped.description: Events the sink could not keep. A sink that reports its own drops is authoritative, so a bounded ring that discarded an old event counts it even though nothing failed.
